analysis|11-12|1918|Η Αυστρία γίνεται δημοκρατία|Austria becomes a republic|After the First World War the Austro-Hungarian Monarchy collapsed, as the nationalities of the empire declared independence. Emperor Charles had already withdrawn from political life, and the German-speaking region was left without a clear political role. The Provisional National Assembly of German Austria took over power. The decision for a republic was taken in the chaos of the collapse, with different political forces coexisting. // On 12 November 1918 the Provisional National Assembly proclaimed the Republic of German Austria. The decision was accompanied by the renunciation by the Habsburgs of any political function. The new republic tried to organize its institutions in conditions of great economic hardship. The new institutions had to deal with hunger, unemployment and the loss of the old markets. // This republic was not easy to sustain, and in the 1930s an authoritarian regime followed. The treaties of Versailles and Saint-Germain forbade union with Germany, but in 1938 Austria was annexed by Nazi Germany. The moment of the proclamation remains important for the history of Austrian political identity. The Austrian republic survived for a short period and was replaced by an authoritarian regime.

analysis|11-12|1927|Εκδιώκεται ο Τρότσκι|Trotsky is expelled|After the death of Lenin in 1924, the Soviet leadership fell into sharp dispute over the succession. Trotsky, one of the main leaders of the October Revolution, clashed with Stalin over the course of the country. Trotsky's opposition pressed for faster industrialization and for more international revolutionary action. Trotsky's expulsion was a key moment, because Stalin used the party machinery to exclude his opponents. // In November 1927 the Central Committee of the Communist Party decided to expel Trotsky from the party. The decision was the last step in a long series of measures against Stalin's opponents. Soon afterwards he was exiled and removed from political life in the country. The opposition could not organize effective resistance, and many of its leaders retreated. // Trotsky's expulsion marked the final triumph of Stalin and the consolidation of his personal power. Trotsky was exiled in 1929 and was later murdered in Mexico in 1940. The episode symbolizes the wave of purges that characterized the Soviet era. The period opened the way to the trials of the 1930s.

analysis|11-12|1940|Η διαταγή του Χίτλερ|Hitler's directive|The Italian attack on Greece had begun in October 1940 and was not going well. Mussolini asked Hitler for help, and Hitler wished to control south-eastern Europe and protect the oil fields of Romania. The balance of the Balkans had become critical for the German plans. Hitler's decision depended on the need to stabilize the southern flank of the Axis before other operations. // On 12 November 1940 Hitler ordered his staff to study a plan for an attack on Greece through Bulgaria. This order prepared the next decisions, and Bulgaria later joined the Axis. The operation eventually took the form of the German invasion in April 1941. The plan included passage through Bulgaria, which was under pressure to take part in the Axis. // This order is significant, because it shows how the Greco-Italian conflict turned into a wider European crisis. Greece resisted the German invasion for a short time, and occupation by the Axis powers followed. The order is a key element for understanding the invasion of the Balkans. Greek resistance was an obstacle to the plans and forms part of the national history of the country.

analysis|11-12|1954|Κλείνει το Έλις Άιλαντ|Ellis Island closes|Ellis Island, in the port of New York, had opened in 1892 as the main reception station for migrants to the United States. Travelers had to pass health examinations and legal checks before entering the country. The island became a symbol of migration, with millions of people passing through it. The change of immigration policy and the development of air transport reduced the importance of the station. // In 1954 the station closed as a place of reception, as migration had changed and air travel had begun to prevail. The buildings remained unused for a time and were later converted into a place of memory. The decision was in essence the end of a great period in the history of American reception. It marked the end of a period in which the port of New York was the first contact of millions of people with America. // Ellis Island remains today an important place of memory for migrants and their descendants. The museum operating there documents the routes of the people who arrived in America. The station is a symbol of the hope and difficulties of migration throughout the history of the United States. Today the island is one of the most visited places of memory in the United States.

analysis|11-12|1990|Ο Τιμ Μπέρνερς-Λι προτείνει το World Wide Web|Tim Berners-Lee proposes the World Wide Web|At CERN in Geneva researchers had great difficulty sharing information, as documents and data were scattered across different systems. Tim Berners-Lee had already paved the way with personal proposals for linking documents. The need for a common information system was becoming ever more pressing. The proposal was not immediately accepted, and it took time for the management of the research centre to accept it. // On 12 November 1990 Berners-Lee, together with Robert Cailliau, submitted a formal proposal for a hypertext system on the internet. The proposal included basic ideas for naming, transfer protocols and the language for describing pages. The idea was to access information in a simple way, from any computer. The first pages ran on a limited number of computers before its use spread across the world. // The World Wide Web came into wide use in the following years, and online communication became everyday practice. This technology changed the economy, education and information across the world. The event is regarded as a milestone in the history of computing, and the technology was not kept as property but as an open standard. The development of the internet brought new forms of communication, commerce and participation.

analysis|11-13|1918|Ο συμμαχικός στόλος μπαίνει στην Κωνσταντινούπολη|The Allied fleet enters Constantinople|After the defeat of the Ottomans in the First World War, the Allies signed an armistice at Mudros on 30 October 1918. The agreement included demilitarization and free passage through the Straits. The Allies considered that Constantinople should be under their control, so that they could supervise the observance of the terms. The presence of the Allied ships was a symbol of the defeat of the Ottoman Empire and of the new balance in the region. // On 13 November 1918 British and French ships anchored in the Bosphorus, and the city came under the control of the Allied forces. Their presence was visible in the heart of the Ottoman capital. The sultan remained in his position, but his authority was now limited. The occupation affected the daily life of the city, with restrictions and control of movements. // The occupation paved the way for the Treaty of Sèvres, which however was not fully implemented. The presence of the Allies strengthened nationalism in Anatolia, and Mustafa Kemal organized the resistance. The event is an important link in the course toward modern Turkish democracy. These developments contributed to the national resistance movement that followed in Anatolia.

analysis|11-13|1940|Πρεμιέρα της ταινίας «Φαντασία» της Ντίσνεϊ|Premiere of Disney's Fantasia|Disney wanted to try new artistic forms in animation, combining images with classical music. The conductor Leopold Stokowski worked with the studio on the choice and recording of the works. The production was ambitious and expensive for its time. The film was part of an experimental project that placed music at the centre of the narrative. // On 13 November 1940 the film was first shown in New York. The film included episodes with works by Bach, Tchaikovsky and Stravinsky, with narrators and images. The sound was presented with a multi-channel system, which was an innovation for cinema halls. The use of classical music in animation was unusual and interested critics and audiences. // The film did not at first have great commercial success, but over time it gained a reputation as an important work of art. Its innovation in sound influenced the development of cinema. Fantasia is regarded today as one of the best-known and most pioneering works of Disney, and its combined approach remains an example of bold creation. The film was later revived in new screenings and reissues. The work is still regarded as an important landmark in the relation of cinema and music in the history of entertainment.

analysis|11-13|1956|Ο φυλετικός διαχωρισμός στα λεωφορεία αντισυνταγματικός|Bus segregation ruled unconstitutional|In Montgomery, Alabama, racial segregation on buses was the law, and African Americans had to give up their seats to white people. After the arrest of Rosa Parks in December 1955 a boycott of the buses had begun, which had significant financial effects on the company. Martin Luther King was one of the main organizers of the movement. This decision followed many reactions and legal proceedings that had begun after Parks's arrest. // On 13 November 1956 the Supreme Court of the United States upheld a decision that found segregation on buses unconstitutional. The decision was based on the principles of equality provided for in the Constitution. This legal victory strengthened the civil rights movement. The judicial victory was important, because it showed the conflict between local law and the federal Constitution. // The boycott ended shortly afterwards, and the abolition of segregation on buses became a fact. The case is linked with the general course of the movement and with the Brown decision of 1954 on schools. The history of Montgomery remains an example of the power of non-violent protest and of the legal struggle. The movement continued with new initiatives in the other fields of public life.

analysis|11-13|2002|Η βύθιση του Prestige|The sinking of the Prestige|The tanker Prestige, flying the flag of the Bahamas, carried heavy fuel oil and belonged to interests managed in Greece. The tanker was old, and the legal responsibility for the maintenance of the ship caused debate. The voyages of such ships along the coasts of Europe had already become the subject of stricter rules. The accident revealed the gaps in the controls of tankers carrying dangerous cargoes to Europe. // In November 2002 the ship faced strong storms and began to leak oil off Galicia. The authorities refused to direct it to a port, and the ship finally sank a few days later. The leak caused enormous pollution on the coasts of Spain and France. The residents and volunteers of Galicia took part en masse in cleaning the coasts. // The accident was one of the largest ecological disasters in the area, with effects on fishing, tourism and marine life. The clean-up of the coasts lasted a long time, with the participation of thousands of volunteers. The incident led to the strengthening of European regulations on tankers. European legislation tightened the safety standards for ships of this type. The episode remains a point of reference for maritime safety and the responsibility of shipowners.

analysis|11-14|1889|Η Νέλι Μπλάι ξεκινά το ταξίδι γύρω από τον κόσμο|Nellie Bly begins her journey around the world|Nellie Bly was a journalist for the New York World, a newspaper that sought unusual stories for its readers. The idea of travelling around the world was inspired by Jules Verne's novel "Around the World in Eighty Days". The journey was a challenge at a time when women rarely travelled alone. Bly's journey became a subject of discussion in the press and of rivals who tried to surpass her. // On 14 November 1889 Bly set out from New York, using ships, trains and other means of transport. The newspaper followed her route, and readers were excited by the news. The journalist completed the route in 72 days, beating the fictional time of the book. During the journey news and impressions were collected, which were published in continuous updates. // The journey was an important event for journalism and for the image of women in public life. Bly became famous, and her achievement inspired many women to pursue similar challenges. Her story remains an example of boldness and independence. Her success opened the way for more women journalists abroad.

analysis|11-14|1910|Η πρώτη απογείωση αεροπλάνου από πλοίο|The first aircraft takeoff from a ship|Aircraft at the beginning of the 20th century were still experimental, but the United States Navy was interested in their use at sea. The idea was that warships could carry and launch aircraft for reconnaissance. Eugene Ely was a pilot who had already taken part in flying displays. The flight was carried out at low speed and over a short route above the surface of the water. // On 14 November 1910 Ely took off from the deck of the cruiser USS Birmingham, which was anchored near Hampton Roads in Virginia. The flight was short, but it showed that the aircraft could take off from a ship. The success was an important test for the future of naval aviation. Ely's success attracted the attention of the navy and led to further experiments. // A few months later Ely landed on a ship, and naval aviation developed into a key element of the fleets. The aircraft carriers that followed changed the strategy of naval warfare. This experiment is regarded as a milestone in the history of aviation and of naval tactics. The aircraft carriers that developed later were based on these first trials.

analysis|11-14|1922|Η πρώτη ημερήσια εκπομπή του BBC|The first daily BBC broadcast|Radio began to spread in Britain in the early 1920s, with amateurs and companies making receivers. A group of companies cooperated to create a single organization, which later became the BBC. The aim of this effort was to organize broadcasting on a national scale. The radio broadcast was created on the basis of the need for a common system that would coordinate the companies of the sector. // On 14 November 1922 the new service began a regular programme of radio broadcasts, with news, music and lectures. The broadcasting was relatively limited, but it addressed a growing audience. The organization of the broadcast was the first step toward institutional radio. Listeners bought receivers and paid a licence fee, and this financed the operation of the station. // The BBC developed into one of the most important public broadcasting organizations in the world. Its character as a public body, financed by listeners' fees, influenced many other systems. This beginning is regarded as the start of a new era in information and entertainment. This structure is regarded as a model for many public media in other countries. The news of the first daily broadcast is regarded as a milestone for public radio in Britain.

analysis|11-14|1969|Εκτοξεύεται ο Απόλλων 12|Apollo 12 Is Launched|The Apollo programme of the United States aimed to bring people to the Moon before the end of the 1960s. After the success of Apollo 11, the second mission aimed to confirm the country's ability for repeated landings. The preparation included extensive tests of the systems and of the trajectory. This mission was part of the wider effort of the United States to prove the reliability of the programme after the first landing. // On 14 November 1969 Apollo 12 was launched from Cape Canaveral, and the mission was the second to set foot on the Moon. The launch was accompanied by lightning, which did not cause serious damage, but forced the technicians to check the systems carefully. The spacecraft continued its journey to the Moon. The landing was made with precision, and the instruments collected data on lunar seismic activity. // The mission finally landed on the Moon, and the astronauts made a walk on the surface and collected samples. The success strengthened confidence in the programme and in its technical capabilities. The mission is important for understanding the development of scientific operations in space. The success of the mission strengthened the next NASA plans for scientific missions.

analysis|11-15|1867|Ο Γεώργιος Α΄ παντρεύεται την Όλγα|George I marries Olga|George I ascended the Greek throne in 1863, as the new king after Otto. Greece had close ties with Russia, which strengthened the Orthodox tradition of the country. Marriage to a member of the Russian imperial family had strong political significance for the state. This marriage took place at a time when Russian influence in Greece was intense. // On 15 November 1867 George I married Grand Duchess Olga Konstantinovna in Saint Petersburg. The marriage strengthened the ties of the Greek royal family with the Russian court. The ceremony was held with great splendour and brought the Greek royal family to the attention of Europe. The royal family was a point of reference for the supporters of the throne and of the Glücksburg dynasty. // The marriage had long-term consequences for Greece's foreign policy and for its relations with the great powers. Olga stayed in Greece and took on a role in the royal family and in society. The event is regarded as an important chapter in the history of the institutionalization of the Greek monarchy. Their descendants took part in important events of European history. This family alliance was linked with the political balances of the era in Europe.

analysis|11-15|1889|Η Βραζιλία γίνεται δημοκρατία|Brazil becomes a republic|Brazil had been an empire under Pedro II since 1831, with a stable and long reign. The abolition of slavery in 1888 caused dissatisfaction among the large landowners, who sought new political leadership. The army was also dissatisfied with the policies of the empire. The fall of the emperor took place with relatively little bloodshed, but it led to profound changes in administration. // On 15 November 1889 Marshal Deodoro da Fonseca organized a military coup in Rio de Janeiro and overthrew Pedro II. The government of the empire ceased to function, and the republic was announced without serious resistance. The emperor left for Europe. The new government drew up a constitution that established the federal form of the state. // This change opened the era of the First Republic in Brazil, with changes in the political system and in constitutional organization. This republic was characterized by the dominance of agrarian elites and by later military interventions. The event remains important in the political history of the country. The first years of the republic were marked by political instability and by the influence of the great landowners. This change laid the basis for the political system that followed in Brazil.

analysis|11-15|1920|Συνεδριάζει η Κοινωνία των Εθνών|The League of Nations holds its first session|After the First World War the victorious powers wanted to create an international organization to prevent new wars. The American president Woodrow Wilson supported the idea of the League of Nations, which was based on the Covenant of the League. The idea was that collective security would limit conflicts. The first sessions of the League showed the will for international consultation, but also the difficulties of cooperation. // On 15 November 1920 the General Assembly of the League of Nations met for the first time in Geneva. The session brought together delegations of many states, although the United States did not officially take part. The organization began to examine questions of peace and cooperation. The absence of the United States from the organization weakened its effectiveness from the start. // The League of Nations did not manage to prevent the Second World War, because of the inability of the great powers to act together. Despite its weaknesses, it laid the foundations for the United Nations, which was founded after the war. Its significance lies in the fact that it established the idea of international cooperation at an institutional level. The experience of the League served as a point of reference for the design of the UN after the Second World War.

analysis|11-16|1532|Ο Πιζάρο συλλαμβάνει τον Αταουάλπα|Pizarro captures Atahualpa|The Inca empire had been exhausted by a civil war between the sons of Huayna Capac, Huascar and Atahualpa. The conflict had strengthened the great lords and left the state divided at the time when the Spaniards arrived. Francisco Pizarro came to the region with a small force of conquistadors, taking advantage of this instability. The discord between the sons of Huayna Capac had left the state without stable leadership and unified administration. // On 16 November 1532 in the city of Cajamarca Pizarro invited Atahualpa to a meeting. When the emperor entered the square with his escort, the Spaniards opened fire and attacked, and captured him without suffering heavy losses. His capture showed that the imperial authority had lost part of its cohesion. The Spaniards used the explicit invitation to a meeting as a trap, which shocked the local leaders. // Atahualpa later promised a great ransom in gold and silver for his freedom, but the Spaniards executed him in 1533. The conquest of Peru followed in the next years, and the Inca empire was overthrown. The episode is regarded as one of the most decisive of the Spanish conquest of America and of the change of balances in the New World. The emperor's capture is one of the most symbolic milestones of the Spanish conquest.

analysis|11-16|1945|Ιδρύεται η UNESCO|UNESCO is founded|After the Second World War the international community was looking for ways to promote peace through cooperation in educational and scientific matters. The idea was that wars begin in the minds of people, and so education and culture were regarded as critical tools. Governments were convened in London to draft the statute of a new organization. The agreement on the establishment of the organization was reached in a climate of optimism after the end of hostilities. // On 16 November 1945 UNESCO, the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization, was officially founded. The statute was signed by many states, and the organization's headquarters were established in Paris. The organization undertook to promote cooperation on questions of education, science, social sciences and cultural heritage. From the start UNESCO operated as a forum for dialogue, where different cultural traditions met for common programmes. // UNESCO became known for programmes to protect monuments and natural sites, with the list of World Heritage sites. Its work influenced education, historical research and the protection of cultural goods throughout the world. Its significance lies in establishing culture as a subject of international cooperation and peace. Today the organization cooperates with hundreds of states and institutions around the world.

analysis|11-18|1883|Οι σιδηρόδρομοι καθιερώνουν ζώνες ώρας|The Railroads Introduce Time Zones|Before 1883 each town in the United States used its own local time, which was determined by the sun. With the development of the railways, timetables became complicated and the differences in time caused confusion. Companies were forced to keep many separate timetables for the same trains. The transition to the new system took place gradually, and some towns reacted because their time changed without warning. // On 18 November 1883 the American railways adopted a system of four time zones, so as to have common timetables across the country. The decision was not legally binding at first, but most towns followed it. The time in each zone was fixed and synchronized with neighboring areas. The idea of time zones was developed by railway engineers and helped improve the organization of transport. // Later the American Congress officially recognized the time zones, and the idea spread to the rest of the world. This arrangement became the foundation of modern international time organization. The history of the time zones shows how transport technology can change the basic daily habits of people. The world later took on its present form of international time organization based on this idea.

analysis|11-18|1928|Η πρεμιέρα του «Steamboat Willie»|Premiere of Steamboat Willie|In the mid-1920s the film industry was experimenting with synchronizing image and sound. Walt Disney and Ub Iwerks had created Oswald the Lucky Rabbit, but Mickey Mouse was a new character. The development of sound technology encouraged companies to try new productions. The film was the first with fully synchronized dialogue and sound effects, which made a great impression on the audience. // On 18 November 1928 the cartoon "Steamboat Willie" premiered in New York, with Mickey Mouse captaining a steamboat. The film had synchronized music and sound effects, which was an innovation for the cartoons of the era. Its success gave Mickey the start of a long career. Mickey Mouse soon appeared in many later cartoons, and the character became recognizable worldwide. // "Steamboat Willie" is regarded as a landmark in the history of animation, because it showed the possibilities of synchronized sound. Mickey Mouse became a symbol of Disney and one of the best-known cartoon figures in the world. The film helped shape the cinema entertainment industry for the following decades. This development established Disney as one of the dominant companies in the sector.

analysis|11-18|1978|Η μαζική αυτοκτονία στο Τζόουνσταουν|The Jonestown mass suicide|Jim Jones founded the religious group "Peoples Temple" in the United States, with a social and utopian message. Over time the group moved to Guyana, to an agricultural community named Jonestown. Jones exercised authoritarian control over the members, and within the community complaints of abuse increased. The community was geographically isolated, which made outside intervention and monitoring of conditions difficult. // In November 1978 an American congressman visited the community to investigate, and with him came journalists and family members. As they were leaving, the congressman and several members were murdered, and Jones asked the others to take poison. Over nine hundred members of the group died, among them many children. Relatives in the United States had begun to ask for help, and this led to the congressman's visit. // The event became one of the most tragic examples of authoritarian religious leadership in modern history. The word "Jonestown" became a synonym for the destructive power of cults. The incident contributed to a re-examination of legislation for the protection of citizens from similar groups. The tragedy prompted discussion about the control of religious groups and the responsibilities of the authorities.

analysis|11-19|1863|Ο λόγος του Γκέτισμπεργκ|The Gettysburg Address|The American Civil War was in a particularly difficult phase in 1863, with huge losses and division within the Union. The battle of Gettysburg in July had cost many lives, and the national cemetery under construction wanted a formal dedication ceremony. Lincoln was asked to speak at the ceremony as president. The speech lasted only two minutes, and for some time the press of the era did not regard it as important as the main speaker. // On 19 November 1863 Lincoln delivered a short speech at Gettysburg in Pennsylvania. The speech linked the sacrifice of the soldiers with the basic principles of democracy and equality that had been founded with the Declaration of Independence. The speech was short, a few minutes, but very powerful in its content. The idea of national unity and equality was expressed in a way that became a model for later political speeches. // The speech soon became one of the best-known texts of American history and is taught in schools all over the world. The idea of a "new birth of freedom" was linked with the later abolition of slavery. The speech is regarded as a point of reference for connecting national unity with human rights. Historians stress that the speech gave a new meaning to the war, beyond its simple military dimension.

analysis|11-19|1969|Ο Apollo 12 προσσεληνώνεται|Apollo 12 lands on the Moon|The Apollo 12 mission aimed to land more precisely than the previous ones, in an area between dark and bright zones of the lunar surface. The plan included a visit to a robotic spacecraft that had landed earlier, Surveyor 3. NASA wanted to examine the endurance of materials after long exposure on the Moon. Surveyor 3 had landed about two years earlier, and the visit to it was very important for the analysis of the soil. // On 19 November 1969 the astronauts Pete Conrad and Alan Bean landed in the Ocean of Storms and made walks on the surface. They visited Surveyor 3 and took parts of it for study on Earth. The walks collected rocks and carried out experiments. The mission used the capability of precise landing to find itself close to the robotic spacecraft. // The success of the mission strengthened confidence in space operations and provided data on the composition of the lunar soil. The comparison of the soil with the robotic spacecraft gave useful results on how materials are affected by space. The mission remains one of the important steps of the Apollo programme. The collection of samples contributed to later studies on the age of lunar rocks.

analysis|11-19|1977|Ο Σαντάτ στην Ιερουσαλήμ|Sadat in Jerusalem|After the Yom Kippur War of 1973, Egypt and Israel were in long-standing tension, without an official peace. President Anwar Sadat sought a way to reach an agreement, despite the reactions of the Arab world. Negotiations with the help of mediators were under way. Sadat's journey caused great upheaval in the Arab world, and several countries broke off relations with Egypt. // On 19 November 1977 Sadat arrived in Jerusalem, and became the first Arab leader to visit Israel. In his speech to the Knesset he spoke of peace and of the recognition of the rights of the two peoples. The visit caused strong reactions in the Arab world and in sections of Israeli public opinion. His presence in Jerusalem was an unprecedented step for the era, with great publicity. // The visit led to the Camp David talks and to the peace agreement of 1979 between Egypt and Israel. Sadat paid for his political daring, as he was assassinated in 1981. The visit is an important milestone in the history of the Middle East. The negotiations that followed led to agreements with international mediation.

analysis|11-20|1945|Αρχίζει η δίκη της Νυρεμβέργης|The Nuremberg trial begins|After the collapse of Nazi Germany in 1945, the victorious Allies decided to try the leading figures of the regime. The idea was to deliver justice for war crimes and crimes against humanity, through a legal process. Nuremberg was chosen as the seat, as the city had a symbolic significance for the Nazi party. The choice of the court rested on a common agreement of the victorious powers, which had been negotiated in London. // On 20 November 1945 the trial of the leading Nazis began in the Palace of Justice of the city. The defendants sat in the dock, among them senior officials, and the trial was reported in the press. The court consisted of judges from the victorious countries. The trial examined evidence from archives and testimonies, and this gave the proceedings the character of a legal review. // The trial established principles of international criminal law, such as the individual responsibility for crimes committed in the name of the state. Some defendants were sentenced to death, and others to imprisonment. The trial is regarded as fundamental for the shaping of modern international justice and human rights. The jurisprudence of the trial influenced later international procedures for war crimes.

analysis|11-20|1985|Η Microsoft κυκλοφορεί τα Windows 1.0|Microsoft releases Windows 1.0|Microsoft sought to bring the graphical environment to personal computers that ran MS-DOS. The competitive pressure from other systems with graphics was great, and the company had announced the idea of Windows two years earlier. The product had to run on compatible PCs without special requirements. The release of Windows 1.0 was delayed considerably compared with the original deadlines, because the software needed more testing. // On 20 November 1985 Windows 1.0 was released, the company's first graphical environment for PC computers. The system provided windows that could be moved and tools such as a calendar and a paint program. The first version was limited and did not have great success in the market. Users had difficulties with speed and with compatibility of applications, so acceptance was limited. // Despite its weaknesses, the graphical environment led to the following versions of Windows, which became the most widespread operating system of the era. This development changed users' habits and established windows as the basic standard on computers. The release of Windows 1.0 is regarded as a milestone in the history of computing. The company improved the system with later versions and gradually won the trust of businesses.

analysis|11-20|1989|Η Σύμβαση για τα Δικαιώματα του Παιδιού|The Convention on the Rights of the Child|The idea that children need special protection and rights had gradually formed in the 20th century. The Declaration of the Rights of the Child of the League of Nations and the Universal Declaration of 1948 had set out basic principles. However, a binding legal text was needed for states. The convention was negotiated for several years with the participation of governments, organizations and experts on childhood issues. // On 20 November 1989 the General Assembly of the UN adopted the Convention on the Rights of the Child, which covers questions of education, health, protection and the participation of children. The Convention gathered wide acceptance and was signed by almost all the states of the world. 20 November was designated as World Children's Day. The convention also contains principles, such as the best interests of the child and the right of the child to be heard. // The Convention is one of the most widely ratified international texts on human rights. It influenced the legislation of many countries and gave children a voice on matters that concern them. Its implementation remains incomplete in many areas, but its existence is an important milestone. Its implementation is monitored by a committee of experts, which examines the reports of the states.

analysis|11-21|1920|Η Ματωμένη Κυριακή του Δουβλίνου|Bloody Sunday in Dublin|Ireland was in a state of war of independence after 1919, with the Irish Republican Army fighting British rule. British forces, together with the Auxiliaries known as the Black and Tans, had intensified their reprisals. The activity of the secret agents of the Irish Army provoked reactions in the British state. The violence of the era had become a daily phenomenon, with attacks and reprisals from both sides. // On 21 November 1920, after the killing of British agents in Dublin, British forces entered Croke Park during a football match and opened fire. The attack killed many spectators and wounded many more. The day became known as "Bloody Sunday". The stadium was full of supporters, and the attack was unannounced and led to panic and victims. // The event provoked anger in Irish public opinion and strengthened support for independence. The violence contributed to the harsher conflict that later led to the treaty of 1921 and the division of the island. Bloody Sunday remains a symbol of the atrocities of the period. The event strengthened international scrutiny of British policy on the island. This episode remains one of the darkest chapters of Irish history.

analysis|11-21|2013|Αρχίζει το Ευρωμαϊντάν|Euromaidan begins|Ukraine stood between the prospect of association with the European Union and close ties with Russia. The government of Viktor Yanukovych had negotiated an association agreement with the EU, which was regarded as politically and economically important. Society was divided, and many expected great changes in the country. The government's decision was perceived by many citizens as a rejection of the European choice of the country. // On 21 November 2013 the government announced that it was suspending the signing of the association agreement with the European Union.
